questionText: How do you record a spam filter in an AI inventory?

answerOptions.text: Record function, version, purpose and owner; check classification against documents
Count every spam filter as an AI system, unchecked
Record only the provider, skip function and version
Never record spam filters; email is never AI

explanation: The product name says neither how the version works nor how the law classifies it. For that, point to vendor documents and the assessing unit.

questionText: You want to draft a private text with an AI assistant. Which selection rule holds?

answerOptions.text: Only paid business tools may write text
If you may share the content and controls, retention and terms fit
Only the best-known product, because the brand guarantees security
No AI tool may be used for writing

explanation: Private use raises the same questions as work. Price and brand say nothing about security, and credentials belong in no prompt.

questionText: A colleague uses suggested replies, a transcription function and a route forecast. What follows for certain?

answerOptions.text: None of the functions can contain AI.
Exactly one function is AI, whatever the product and version.
Automatically exactly three standalone AI systems in law
Functions and versions go in the inventory; their classification gets checked

explanation: AI functions often sit inside everyday products. You record function and version, then check how many standalone systems there are.

questionText: Why does a maintained inventory of the AI functions and systems in use matter?

answerOptions.text: It is needed for the tax return.
It is the reviewable basis for risk assessment, rules and ownership
It is mandatory only for companies with more than 250 employees.
Its sole purpose is IT budget planning.

explanation: Without an inventory there is no sound risk assessment, ownership or approval. Whether and how the law requires one depends on system and role.

questionText: An employee wants to process a customer list with names and email addresses in an unapproved AI service. What holds?

answerOptions.text: Business contact details are always unrestricted.
A paid account is legal basis enough.
Stop until purpose, legal basis, data class, minimization and approval are clear
Digitally stored data may not be processed.

explanation: Names and email addresses can be personal data. A DPA alone does not make processing lawful.

questionText: Which basis is enough to approve an AI workflow?

answerOptions.text: The product name contains the word Enterprise.
Documented review of purpose, data class, feature, contract, configuration, permissions, retention
The provider excludes customer data from training by default.
The system runs on a local machine.

explanation: An approval covers one combination of purpose, data, feature and configuration. "Enterprise" in the name or a local machine checks none of it.

questionText: Why must unapproved consumer offers not be used with company data?

answerOptions.text: Because their answers are worse than the paid versions.
Because a reviewed contract, data controls and documented approval are usually missing
Because they work in English only.
Because they need no internet connection.

explanation: Without a reviewed DPA, binding data controls and an agreed data region, using personal company data can be unlawful.

questionText: A colleague wants to analyse a supplier list with company names, contacts and purchasing terms. What holds?

answerOptions.text: Allowed as soon as an enterprise product is used
Always prohibited, whatever the purpose and approved workflow
Check purpose, personal data, confidentiality, minimization and approval before input
Supplier data may never go into an AI tool.

explanation: The company name can be public, the contact personal data, the terms a trade secret. So the approval of purpose, data and system decides.

questionText: What is the main difference between a good prompt and a bad one?

answerOptions.text: A good prompt is longer than 500 words.
It names task, inputs, format, limits and how to handle gaps
A good prompt uses English technical terms.
A good prompt always starts with 'Please'.

explanation: Clear inputs and limits make the output checkable; a role is optional. Even a precise prompt guarantees neither correctness nor completeness.

questionText: An AI assistant drafts an email to an important customer for you. It sounds professional. What do you do next?

answerOptions.text: Send it at once; AI assistants make no email mistakes
Check facts, sources, completeness, your authority, recipients and required approval
Have a second AI tool check the text.
Send it next week to gain some distance

explanation: A professional tone proves nothing. Check sources, gaps, commitments and recipients according to the impact; a second AI tool is no review.

questionText: Which constraint should a good prompt for an email template carry?

answerOptions.text: 'Only supplied facts, mark gaps, no unauthorized commitments'
'Write at least 1,000 words'.
'Use emojis to sound friendly'.
'Include as many technical terms as possible'.

explanation: That shows what the assistant invented and keeps commitments small. It does not replace specialist review.

questionText: You have an AI assistant turn your meeting notes into minutes. They include a point that was never discussed. What do you do?

answerOptions.text: Keep it; the AI may have caught something you missed
Check it against the primary source, cut unsupported content, tighten the prompt
Discard the whole record and write it by hand
Add a question mark and send it to everyone

explanation: Models sometimes add what the source does not contain. A tighter instruction only makes that rarer, so the source check stays.

questionText: What is an AI hallucination?

answerOptions.text: A technical system error in which the AI crashes.
A plausible-sounding output that is unsupported or wrong.
Deliberate manipulation by hackers.
A visual error in the user interface.

explanation: A language model produces token sequences without checking facts automatically. So every claim a decision depends on goes back to a suitable source.

questionText: Copilot's market analysis says the German AI market grew by 34.2% to EUR 12.8 billion in 2025 (source: Bitkom 2025). How do you check it?

answerOptions.text: The figure sounds plausible, that is enough.
Open the Bitkom website and look for the named study
Ask ChatGPT whether the figure is right.
Replace the figure with your own estimate.

explanation: Figure and citation can be generated without the study existing. Check definition, period and calculation in the primary source, not with ChatGPT.

questionText: Which use needs specialist and organizational controls beyond a simple output review?

answerOptions.text: Writing an internal newsletter piece.
Legal assessments, medical advice, decisions with serious consequences for people
Translating an email from German into English.
Building an agenda for a team meeting.

explanation: Legal, medical and employment decisions can have serious consequences. They need qualified accountability, suitable sources and, case by case, special controls.

questionText: Copilot's summary of a 45-minute Teams meeting records a project start on 1 June. You remember the date stayed open. What follows?

answerOptions.text: Copilot is probably right; it analysed the whole audio
The date stays open until the transcript or confirmed notes support it
It was probably set while you were briefly distracted
Copilot invents no concrete dates, so the date is right.

explanation: Neither memory nor summary is primary evidence. The participants confirm the record against the transcript or notes.

questionText: Which of the following belongs in an AI usage policy?

answerOptions.text: A technical explanation of how neural networks work.
Approval matrix with purpose, version, feature, data classes, configuration, owners, review status
The full original text of the EU AI Act.
Instructions for programming AI models.

explanation: A policy governs approvals, with review duties, incident reporting, ownership and review triggers.

questionText: What does Article 4 of the EU AI Act require from companies that use AI systems?

answerOptions.text: A computer science degree for every employee
Measures supporting AI literacy development in people acting on their behalf
AI use by the IT department only
An annual AI audit by external auditors

explanation: Article 4 has applied since 2 February 2025; as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, it requires supporting measures that consider knowledge, experience, training, use context and the people affected. It prescribes no attestation.

questionText: An employee accidentally enters payroll data into an AI service. What is the right first step?

answerOptions.text: Wait and see whether anyone notices.
Delete the chat history and tell nobody.
Report at once via the incident channel, preserve evidence, let owners assess
Ask the provider for a legal assessment, report nothing internally

explanation: The controller assesses whether a notifiable personal data breach exists. Four- or 24-hour stages are set by the organization; the law does not prescribe them.

questionText: A new AI tool, say an industry chatbot, is to be introduced. An AI usage policy already exists. What has to happen?

answerOptions.text: Nothing; the existing policy covers new tools automatically
Review purpose, data, contract, configuration, risks first; update inventory and approval matrix
Trial it with real data until the next review
Only inform IT; the policy stays unchanged

explanation: A new product or feature triggers a review. The decision is recorded before real data goes in.
